description: SDXL's CLIP-G text encoder, in its two shipped packagings: the diffusers split (`q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj`) and the single-file OpenCLIP fusion (`in_proj_weight`). Contiguous thirds, T2 — the derive is manifest range-slicing over the same chunks, which is what makes single-file <-> diffusers conversion of the CLIP-G tensors a run-preserving derive rather than a refusal. SCOPED to text_encoder_2: CLIP-L ships the same key spellings at 768 and is a different component with its own packaging.
name: sdxl.clip-g-split-to-fused
provenance: tensorfs#127 CLOSES HERE. v1 could not say whether a document was a SERVE LANE or a FRAGMENT, and only an accident distinguished them — the CLIP-G pair were fragments that a `lanes=` header must never name. In v2 a fragment is not a document kind at all: it is this, a morphism between two topologies, and only topologies can be named by a lane.

seams.provenance: RATIFIED, transplanted from the v1 fragments `sdxl.clip-g-fused-qkv@1` and `sdxl.clip-g-split-qkv@1`, which this morphism replaces — the design's ruling that a FRAGMENT is a morphism seam file, not a serve lane. OpenCLIP text encoders store attention as nn.MultiheadAttention's fused `in_proj_weight`, equal thirds in q, k, v order; diffusers' CLIPTextModel splits them. Measured against the real SDXL header: each projection is [1280, 1280] and the fusion is [3840, 1280].
RATIFIED with the weight seam above: the bias splits the same way, three [1280] parts concatenating to [3840], in q, k, v order. Same citation — OpenCLIP's nn.MultiheadAttention in_proj layout.
